provenance: Telephone call, 2026-09-01, Larry's son asking the four cold interview probes written the same day and typing Larry's answers as he spoke them. Nothing from the day's document research was supplied to him before he answered. Raw capture and analysis: research/interviews/2026-09-01-phone-answers.md.
text: The best place to have readios because it was high. All of that area about 100 miles around it was all at surface of water, or 3 feet above water. Everything was all swamp, except the mountain went up 2900 square feet. They (the people at the camp at Dong Xoai, special forces team, there were about 16 people, they were attacked by about 4000 enemy all at once at 4am in the morning, I was sitting at the radio when it happened, guy on radio was dying from shot in the stomach, Gagne was with me and died, he was a french foreign Legionair) could get us on the radio and were like 40 miles away, could transmit 25 miles but with being on the mouttain and on the curvature of the Earth allow the signal to connect.
researchNotes: The parenthesis is his son's inserted context around Larry's words; everything here is Larry's own account as spoken. Asked only what the camp was there for, with no phrase offered and no alternatives to choose from, he named the mission and then explained the physics himself. The RADIX Press order of battle, read hours earlier and never shown to him, prints the camp's official mission as "MISSION: RADIO RELAY" (sources/radix-sf-order-of-battle). His testimony and the official designation agree. He also volunteered, unasked, an account of being at a radio during the attack on the Special Forces camp at Đồng Xoài, and named Gagne, who appears nowhere else in this archive. Tensions held open rather than resolved: a UTT/68th Aviation Company memoir found the same day has that camp's radio officer rescued alive, while Larry remembers the man on the radio dying of a stomach wound; the published battle opened on the night of 9 June 1965, and he says 4 a.m. Whether Larry was on the mountain or at the Saigon end when the call came is not stated and is in the interview guide. His "2900 square feet" is his own rendering and is preserved; the summit stands about 986 metres.
